The first frost arrived three weeks early this year, which means the last of the dahlias came out of the ground on a Sunday morning in a hurry rather than on a calm afternoon in November. Here is how I store the tubers over winter, and what went wrong the year I didn’t.
![Dahlia tubers drying on newspaper](https://allotment-notes.example/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/tubers-1024x768.jpg)
Caption: Drying on newspaper in the shed for a week.
### Lifting
Cut the stems down to a hand’s length, then lift each clump with a fork from well outside the stem so you don’t spear the tubers. Shake off the loose soil, but don’t wash them; a little dry soil helps them keep.
### Storing
1. Leave them upside down for a few days so water drains out of the hollow stems.
2. Pack them in a crate of dry compost or sawdust, crowns up.
3. Keep the crate somewhere cool and frost-free, and check them once a month.
The year I skipped the draining step, half of them rotted by January. The crowns had held water, and that was enough. Now I label every crate with the variety and the date, because by spring I never remember which brown lump is which.
